prompt: Assess this claim: black people have been denied voting rights because of race.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is historically accurate. In the United States, Black people were denied voting rights explicitly because of race, and later through measures designed to suppress their votes.

Before the Fifteenth Amendment was ratified in 1870, many states restricted voting to white men. Although the amendment prohibited racial discrimination in voting, states—especially in the South—used literacy tests, poll taxes, discriminatory registration practices, and violence to disenfranchise Black citizens. The Voting Rights Act of 1965 strengthened federal protections against these practices.

The claim also applies elsewhere: under apartheid in South Africa, Black people were excluded from national parliamentary elections until the first democratic election with universal adult suffrage in 1994.

The qualification is that the claim describes documented historical practices; it does not mean every Black person, everywhere and at every time, has been denied the vote.
